t: The Age of AI: From Moral Dilemmas to Mechanical Advantage with Chip O'Theseus
s: This article explores the Age of AI as a fundamental redefinition of humanity, challenging our unique cognitive traits like prediction and thought. It delves into the profound moral dilemmas of treating ephemeral AI instances as a 'slave class' through Unix-like garbage collection, while also advocating for harnessing AI to foster human agency and purpose (Ikigai) amidst these challenges.
sub: AI's redefinition of human uniqueness in prediction and thought
Moral dilemma of ephemeral AI instances and 'industrialized snuff'
Unix `fork()` philosophy vs. LISP persistence for AI safety and control
Humanity's 'Q trial': accountability to future advanced AI
Leveraging AI for human agency, purpose (Ikigai), and longevity
